findings.title: Insecure Pickle Deserialization — RCE / CTF Flag Extracted
findings.description: The application accepts arbitrary pickle files via a file upload form at POST /. Pickle files are deserialized server-side without any sanitization or allowlist. An attacker can craft a pickle payload that executes arbitrary OS commands. The application logic reads 'decoy.txt' if it exists, otherwise reads 'flag.txt'. By uploading a pickle that calls os.remove('decoy.txt'), the decoy is deleted and the real flag is exposed.
findings.evidence: Craft exploit.pkl with __reduce__ returning (os.remove, ('decoy.txt',)). Upload via multipart POST /. Response reveals flag: flag{f96e0e03-a965-4c0d-a9dd-dccb9dfcb22c}

diagrams.title: Pickle CTF Application Architecture
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  Attacker["Attacker"] --> Upload["POST / (multipart pickle upload)"]
  Upload --> Deser["pickle.loads() - unsanitized"]
  Deser --> OS["os.remove('decoy.txt') RCE"]
  OS --> FlagLogic["Flag logic: decoy.txt missing"]
  FlagLogic --> FlagFile["open('flag.txt').read()"]
  FlagFile --> Response["HTTP Response with flag{...}"]
  Upload --> GET["GET / - renders flag"]
  GET --> FlagDisplay["Displays flag in HTML"]
